full_judgment: 12. In the case reported in 33 DLR 207 the decree holders obtained the decree for permanent injunction against the judgment-debtors who were permanently restrained from creating any disturbance to the peaceful possession of the suit land by the decree-holders but the judgment-debtors violated the order of permanent injunction and trespassed into the suit land and cultivated Boro paddy therein. The decree holders prayed for enforcement of the decree by putting the judgment-debtors into the civil jail and by attaching their properties under Order XXI rule 32 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Munsif allowed the prayer of the decree-holders and committed the judgment-debtors to the civil prison to suffer imprisonment for 15 days each. Thereafter the judgment-debtors moved this Court in revision and obtained a Rule. In course of hearing of the Rule it was submitted on behalf of the judgment-debtors that the Miscellaneous Case was not maintainable on the ground that when a prohibitory order of injunction was violated the decree was not executable and referred to the case reported in 16 DLR 61 in support of their contention. Mustafa Kamal J held that sub-rule(1) of rule 32 of Order XXI was a particular manner or method of enforcing an otherwise in executable decree in case of violation and sub-rule (1) implies that if the prohibitory order is violated then by securing the detention of judgment-debtor in the civil prison or attaching his properties or by both such an in executable decree can be enforced and that sub-rule (5) is an alternative or additional remedy. Secondly, the words "willfully failed to obey" do not imply that it is only a negative act of willful failure that will attract the mischief of sub-rule (1). If a person does exactly the act which he is prohibited from doing then it is very much a willful failure to obey the decree. Thirdly, when a prohibitory order of injunction is violated the decree can be enforced invoking provision of sub-rule (1) of rule 32. Sub-rule (1) of rule 32 is a special penalty reserved for the judgment-debtor if he willfully disobeyed the decree. Fourthly, there is a remedy for every wrong done and if a prohibitory order of injunction cannot be enforced it would be practically useless to obtain such a decree for permanent injunction. His Lordship thereafter referred to the cases of Prag Dutt Vs. Kedar Nath and others 1945 AIR Oudh 81, and the case of Gundila Manjappa Shelly Vs. Manjakke Shedthi and others reported in 1961 AIR Mysore 268 wherein it has been held that a person disobeys an injunction not only if he fails to perform an act which he is directed to do also when he does an act which he is prohibited from doing; and his Lordship also referred to the case of Toon Lal Vs. Soonoo Lal reported in 1938 AlR Pat 522; the case of Nari Chinnabba Chetty Vs. E Chengalroya Chetty and others reported in 1950 AlR Madras 237; the case of Ajabroo Vs. Atmaram, reported in 1954 AlR Nag 245; the case of Muuari Lal Vs. Nawal Kishore reported in 1961 AlR Pur 547 and the case of Saleh Ahmed Vs. Kabir Ahmed reported in 13 DLR (Dhaka) 531 and held, contrary to the views taken in the case reported in 16 DLR 61, that when a prohibitory injunction is violated the decree-holder's remedy lies in the enforcement of the decree under Order XXI rule 32 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure apart from any other remedy that he may have had.
